conviction_note: No option chain, one analyst (Cantor, also the September placement agent) and turnover of roughly $12-25k a day. The evidence is a set of small, mostly offsetting items: a revenue bar that probably sits above the run rate, a liquidity squeeze (H1 cash halved, five ABL amendments, a $6M PIPE), a coming resale overhang, against insiders buying at $2.83 and EBITDA guided up. The name has fallen on all five prints in the baseline (median -2.26%). That gives p_up 45 on an abs_move of 7, which works out to -0.7, close to the findings' own sum of -1.1. Both are small because no single item decides the print.
bar: Disputed and thin. Q3 2026 revenue estimates: about $198M (stockalarm, via search snippet) against $204.6M (chartmill, via search snippet, 403 on fetch). Both trace to about one analyst, Cantor Fitzgerald, Buy, $5 PT (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/xbp/forecast/ via search). No company guidance number exists. The only company statement is 'We expect an inflection in our revenue in the second half of the year' (Q2 call, 2026-08-13, https://www.webull.com/news/15397668849148928). The run rate is Q1 $197.1M and Q2 $191.3M. Q3 2025 pro forma was $220.4M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1839530/000110465925112647/xbp-20251114xex99d1.htm). EarningsWhispers shows no consensus (https://earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/XBP/202606). Because the bar is unsourced to two agreeing estimates, every finding that depends on it is capped small.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest was 14,984 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, down 4,922, with 1.85 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/xbp/short-interest). Against 14,156,584 shares outstanding (S-3, 2026-09-22) that is about 0.1%, so the stock is not a crowded short. The next settlement (Nov 13) publishes Nov 24, after the window. There is no options market, so no skew. Baseline tape: spot 2.815, 5d -3.1%, 20d -0.53%, -66.8% from the 52-week high, 20-day average volume about 4,163 shares (about $12k a day). Concentrated holders: Cantor and affiliates 7.2% (13D/A, 2026-09-22), plus the Avenue funds (also lenders) and HGM/HCI (Chadha).

findings.finding: Management promised a second-half 2026 revenue inflection on the Q2 call, but the run rate is falling sequentially: Q1 $197.1M, Q2 $191.3M (-2.9% QoQ, -14.0% YoY pro forma). The sell-side numbers I could find ($198M and $204.6M, one analyst) sit 3-7% above Q2. Flat sequential revenue near $191-195M would be about -12% against the $220.4M Q3 2025 pro forma base: a narrower YoY decline, but likely a miss against the lone estimate and not a visible 'inflection'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (revenue -14% YoY, record margin, bookings +52%) closed -2.26%. Q1 2026 closed -9.4%. All 5 prints in the baseline closed down. No estimate existed for those prints, so there is no clean beat/miss history.
findings.why_not_priced: No published consensus is tracked (EarningsWhispers blank) and nobody asked questions on the Q2 call (operator: no questions). If the market held a view on whether the 'inflection' arrives in Q3, a second estimate would exist and the stock would not trade on about $12k a day. Capped small because the bar is disputed.
findings.independence: Q1/Q2 revenue from the 10-Qs (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/XBP/10-q-xbp-global-holdings-inc-quarterly-earnings-report-40f8a6f733be.html; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1839530/000110465926097350/xbp-20260630x10q.htm). Q3 2025 pro forma base from the 2025-11-14 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1839530/000110465925112647/xbp-20251114xex99d1.htm). These are different documents from the call.

findings.finding: Liquidity is tightening, and Q3's balance sheet will show it. Cash fell from $37.1M (12/31/25) to $18.6M (6/30/26) and restricted cash from $31.6M to $9.4M. Current liabilities were $307.9M against $196.8M of current assets. Total debt is about $372.9M against a roughly $40M market cap. The MidCap ABL was amended five times between Dec 2025 and May 2026, and the European senior facilities breached leverage and interest-coverage covenants at 3/31/26 (waived 5/13/26). The company then raised only $6.05M in a September PIPE at $2.55-2.83 with no stated use of proceeds. No 2026 filing contains 'substantial doubt' (EDGAR full-text search, 0 hits).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (European covenant breach and waiver disclosed in the 10-Q) closed -9.4%. Q2 2026 (cash halved year to date) closed -2.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is 67% off its high and the equity is a thin sliver over $373M of debt. What is not yet visible is the Q3 cash level after the PIPE and whether another waiver or amendment was needed for Q3 covenants. If that were priced, the September PIPE would not have cleared at a premium tier for insiders. Lesson 4 answer: the money's use is unstated, and there is no bookings ramp needing working capital beyond the TCV growth. Covenant pressure is documented, so the sign is negative but small, because there is no going-concern flag.
findings.independence: The covenant breach and waiver come from the Q1 10-Q summary (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/XBP/10-q-xbp-global-holdings-inc-quarterly-earnings-report-40f8a6f733be.html). The fifth ABL amendment is exhibit 10.1 to the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1839530/000110465926097350/xbp-20260630xex10d1.htm). The PIPE is in the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1839530/000110465926107322/tm2623653d2_8k.htm). Shares a filing with the revenue finding (the Q2 10-Q) but a different line.

findings.finding: In the September 11 PIPE, insiders and a lender paid the top tier, $2.83, against $2.55 for outside funds: CEO Jonovic (31,500 shares), CFO Avramovic (8,833), the Chairman's HCI (204,946) and the Avenue funds (600,000; Avenue also holds 2030 notes and the super-senior term loan). Spot is $2.815, below the price insiders paid two months before a print they had visibility into.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior insider-buying episode around a print in the baseline. Insider Form 4s in May 2026 preceded the Q1 print, which closed -9.4% (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001839530.json).
findings.why_not_priced: Public since September and the stock has drifted from $3.17 (9/21) to $2.815, so the market has not paid for the signal. If it had, the price would sit at or above the insiders' $2.83. The signal is small: the dollar amounts are modest, and Avenue is protecting a credit position.
findings.independence: The S-3 selling-stockholder table confirms the purchasers (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1839530/000110465926109672/tm2625897d1_s3.htm). Same transaction as the financing finding, read for a different signal (who paid what) rather than for the cash.

findings.finding: Resale overhang: 2,275,245 PIPE shares (about 16% of the 14.16M outstanding) are registered for resale on the S-3 filed 2026-09-22. Alyeska (784,313), Citadel CEMF (392,156) and Cantor (196,078) bought at $2.55, about 10% under spot. The insider lock-up ran to the earlier of 60 days after the ~9/15 closing (~11/14) or 30 days after effectiveness, so it has ended or ends around now. Against about 4,000-8,000 shares of daily volume, any selling into post-print liquidity weighs on the stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior resale-overhang episode in the baseline. The stock fell from $3.17 on 9/21 to $2.815 during the registration period.
findings.why_not_priced: The overhang is public. What is unpriced is that the print day brings the volume these holders need to exit, in a stock that otherwise trades a few thousand shares. I did not confirm whether the S-3 has been declared effective (no EFFECT notice in the last 30 submissions), which keeps this small.
findings.independence: The lock-up terms come from the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1839530/000110465926107322/tm2623653d2_8k.htm) and Cantor's holding from its 13D/A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1839530/000121390026102187/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml). All rest on the same PIPE.

findings.finding: Margin trajectory: normalized EBITDA rose from about $15.6M (Q1) to $21.9M (Q2, 11.5% margin, +40.6% QoQ) and adjusted gross margin to a record 24.9%. Management raised its annualized efficiency target to $65-75M (about $35M in 2026) and guided EBITDA growth into 2H26. The Q3 2025 pro forma adjusted EBITDA comparison is $24.7M, so about $23-25M would be roughly flat YoY on revenue down about 12%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 delivered a record margin, EBITDA +8.4% YoY and +40.6% QoQ, and the stock closed -2.26%. The name has not paid for margin beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely inside what management guided ('normalized EBITDA growth into the second half'), so this is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect. Sized small because the name sold the last margin beat.
findings.independence: The peer Conduent's Q3 2026 (11/5) adjusted EBITDA was +16.1% on cost cuts with revenue -11.7%, the same shrink-to-margin pattern (https://finviz.com/news/417747/conduent-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-reaffirms-2026-outlook-bolsters-liquidity-position-and-completes-transit-sale). This is a proxy.

findings.finding: Peer read-through: Conduent (BPO, government and commercial transaction processing) reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-05. Revenue was $534M (-11.7% YoY, +0.6% QoQ, 2.1% below consensus), new business ACV signings fell 12.9%, operating cash flow was -$107M, and the adjusted loss missed. Revenue was stable sequentially but bookings were weak, and the press coverage was headlined 'misses'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No XBP history of trading on peer prints. XBP's own bookings were +51.6% YoY in Q2, the opposite of Conduent's.
findings.why_not_priced: This peer printed after XBP last spoke, and XBP's thin estimate is unlikely to have been revised. It is an industry proxy, not XBP's number, so it is small.

findings.finding: Executive Chairman Par Chadha (head of HGM, whose affiliate HCI bought in the PIPE) told the company on 2026-10-20 that he will not stand for re-election, 'not the result of any disagreement'. This comes while a strategic-alternatives process with a financial advisor (announced May 2026) is open with no update. The release or call may carry a strategic-review update in either direction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The strategic alternatives announcement came with the Q1 print (2026-05-14), which closed -9.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: An 8-K with no press coverage and no analyst questions. A founder-chairman stepping back mid-review is ambiguous: it could mean the review is not producing a whole-company buyer, or it could precede a transaction. The range is wide and the centre near zero.
findings.independence: The strategic alternatives release (https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/XBP/pressreleases/1971740/xbp-global-announces-exploration-of-strategic-alternatives-to-enhance-value-for-all-stakeholders/) and the Q2 call note that an advisor was engaged (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-0-1999012-20260814).

outside_window.finding: The next FINRA short-interest settlement (2026-11-13) publishes about 2026-11-24, after the exit, so any post-PIPE hedging by the $2.55 buyers is not visible inside the window.

rejected_candidates.candidate: FY2026 revenue estimate of $858.2M (stockanalysis), which would imply about $235M a quarter in H2
rejected_candidates.detail: Inconsistent with the 10-Q run rate (H1 $388.4M), and the page cites 22 analysts against the 1 every other source shows. It looks like stale pre-merger data and was not used as the bar.
The same single Cantor rating already in `bar`. Cantor is also the PIPE placement agent and a 7.2% holder.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q2 bookings strength (TCV $121.3M, +51.6%; new ACV $36M, +57%; $2.5B pipeline flat) as support for a 2H revenue inflection
rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the revenue-inflection finding (same call, same line). Bookings convert over quarters, so this offsets the miss risk rather than adding a separate positive.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The small negative lean matches the run-up (-3.1% over 5 days) and the reaction history (0 of 5 up), so it is partly priced, which keeps p_up at 45 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6, bar unsourced or disputed (one analyst, $198M vs $204.6M): revenue finding capped from -0.5 to -0.3
Lesson 4, financing as a question: the use of proceeds is unstated and there is documented covenant pressure but no going-concern flag. Sign kept negative, size eased from -1.0 to -0.8
Lesson 1, the name sells its beats (Q2 record margin closed -2.26%): margin finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3
Lesson 5 (positioning in a microcap is the information set, not a cause): resale-overhang finding cut from -0.5 to -0.3
Insider-buying finding trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4 because it has been public since September (my own caveat)
Lesson 8, thin coverage: abs_move_pct raised from 6 to 7
